title: Catastrophic Forgetting in LLMs
description: A study of catastrophic forgetting when GPT-2 small & medium is fine-tuned on the DailyDialog conversational dataset. Factual knowledge retention is tracked across training checkpoints using a QA benchmark derived from LAMA T-REx. The pipeline measures Knowledge Retention Rate, Fact Frequency Robustness (rare vs. common facts), and representation drift via cosine similarity of hidden states.

title: Compute-Optimal Tiny Transformers
description: Replicating Chinchilla scaling laws at miniature scale. Tiny GPT-like models (12K–800K parameters) are trained on WikiText-103 across nine iso-compute FLOP budgets, with multiple seeds and two learning-rate schedules (matched and fixed-horizon). Validation losses are aggregated and fit to Chinchilla-style parametric loss surfaces, recovering compute-optimal model-size-to-token ratios and power-law scaling curves at small scale.

title: Conversational AutoML
description: An agentic system that runs automated machine learning on tabular data in response to natural-language questions. Six specialized agents — orchestration, feature engineering, a feature critic, analysis, a previous-results explainer, and a conversation meta-agent — interpret the user's intent, profile and preprocess the data, propose domain-agnostic feature transformations, and train a diverse set of candidate models evaluated by cross-validation, then explain the results conversationally. Multi-turn conversations track and reuse prior runs to avoid redundant retraining on follow-up questions.

title: Are LLM Circuits Stable Under Prompt Variance?
description: A mechanistic interpretability study probing whether the internal circuits a transformer uses to solve a task stay consistent when the prompt is reworded. Across a battery of prompt variants, circuit components and activation patterns are extracted and compared to test how robust learned circuits are to surface-level input changes — a question that bears directly on model interpretability and reliability. Built as the final project for the Deep Learning Using Transformers course at Johns Hopkins University.

title: Minesweeper with Deep Q-Networks
description: A deep reinforcement learning agent that learns to play Minesweeper, navigating the game's partially observable, stochastic board to uncover safe cells while avoiding mines. A Deep Q-Network (DQN) pairs Q-learning with a neural network to learn a move policy directly from board state, extending DQN beyond the usual Atari benchmarks to a puzzle domain dominated by uncertainty. Accompanied by a written report, "Navigating Stochastic Environments with Deep Q Networks."
